Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization for total hip replacement  
CPT 27130  
Reference number: POC-2FE0EDCD1B-73051  

Dear Member Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for total hip replacement, CPT 27130. The stated reason for denial is that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment.

The clinical record documents extensive conservative treatment and failure to obtain adequate relief:

- I have experienced 18 months of progressive hip pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy from February 20, 2026, through June 12, 2026, including 16 visits. Treatment focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait. The completed course is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on March 21, 2026. It provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, I continue to have substantial pain and functional impairment.

The record also documents objective disease and significant loss of function supporting the requested surgery:

- A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated June 13, 2026, showed superolateral joint-space narrowing to 1 mm, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophytes.
- I require a cane for ambulation and can walk only one block.
- I cannot put on my shoes without assistance.
- Provocative testing is positive on the affected side, and range of motion is limited by pain.

The submitted information therefore demonstrates that conservative treatment was not merely attempted but completed over an extended period and included supervised physical therapy, medication, and injection treatment. These measures failed to provide durable relief. The imaging findings and functional limitations further demonstrate that the condition remains clinically significant and materially interferes with daily activities.

The record also identifies no documented contraindication to surgery. There is no active infection or untreated substance use disorder. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

I request reversal of the denial and authorization for CPT 27130. Alternatively, please arrange an expedited peer-to-peer review with Duval, MD, the treating orthopedic surgeon.

I also request that Independence Blue Cross provide the specific medical policy and clinical review criteria actually applied to this request, including the policy title, policy number, applicable version or effective date, and the precise criteria used to determine that the documented conservative treatment was inadequate. The public materials reviewed for this appeal did not identify the payer-specific governing policy for CPT 27130, so this appeal does not quote or rely on an unverified policy.

Please consider the enclosed clinical records, including the physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection history, radiology report, examination findings, and functional limitations. Please send the appeal determination and the criteria applied in writing.

Sincerely,

Taylor Ellison  

Enclosures:  
- Physical therapy discharge note  
- Medication and treatment history  
- Corticosteroid injection record  
- June 13, 2026, radiology report  
- Orthopedic examination and clinical notes  
- Prior authorization denial notice
